solution: Here \(X=\{1,2,3,4\}\). Reflexivity needs \((i,i)\in R\) for every element, but \((4,4)\notin R\), so R is not reflexive. R is symmetric: each off-diagonal pair appears with its reverse (\((1,2),(2,1)\) and \((2,3),(3,2)\)). R is not transitive: \((1,2)\in R\) and \((2,3)\in R\) but \((1,3)\notin R\). Therefore R is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive. Hence option D.

For the equilateral triangle with vertices \((0,0),(p,1),(1,q)\), equate the two sides from the origin: \(p^2+1 = 1+q^2\), giving \(p=q\). Equate a side to the remaining side: \(2(1-p)^2 = p^2+1\), i.e. \(p^2-4p+1=0\), so \(p = 2-\sqrt{3}\) (the root in \((0,1)\)). Then \(p+q = 2(2-\sqrt{3}) = 4-2\sqrt{3}\). Hence option D. Option C, \(2-\sqrt{3}\), is the value of \(p\) alone, not \(p+q\).

With the right angle at B, \(\vec{BA}\cdot\vec{BC}=0\). Here \(\vec{BA}=A-B=(k-2k,\ 1-0,\ -1-2)=(-k,1,-3)\) and \(\vec{BC}=C-B=(2,\ k,\ -1)\). Then \(\vec{BA}\cdot\vec{BC} = -2k+k+3 = -k+3 = 0\), so \(k=3\). Hence option D.

The modal class is \(164\text{--}166\) (highest frequency \(24\)). Using the mode formula with \(L=164,\ f_1=24,\ f_0=15,\ f_2=13,\ h=2\): \(\text{Mode} = L + \dfrac{f_1-f_0}{2f_1-f_0-f_2}\cdot h = 164 + \dfrac{9}{20}\cdot 2 = 164.9\) cm. Hence option D.

Let \(x=\sin\theta\), so \(\sin^{-1}x=\theta\) and \(\sqrt{1-x^2}=\cos\theta\). Then \(y = \dfrac{\theta\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} + \ln(\cos\theta) = \theta\tan\theta + \ln(\cos\theta)\). Differentiating with respect to \(\theta\): \(\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = \tan\theta + \theta\sec^2\theta - \tan\theta = \theta\sec^2\theta\). Since \(\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=\cos\theta\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\theta\sec^2\theta}{\cos\theta} = \theta\sec^3\theta\). Hence option C.

The angles are in the ratio \(3:5:4\); since \(3+5+4=12\) parts \(=180^\circ\), \(A=45^\circ,\ B=75^\circ,\ C=60^\circ\). By the law of sines \(a=k\sin A,\ b=k\sin B,\ c=k\sin C\). Then \(a+b+\sqrt{2}\,c = k\big(\sin 45^\circ + \sin 75^\circ + \sqrt{2}\sin 60^\circ\big) = k\Big(\tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + \tfrac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4} + \tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\Big) = \tfrac{3k(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6})}{4} = 3k\sin 75^\circ = 3b\). Hence option C.
